hero.filename: Rocky Mount Amtrak-ACL Station; Trackside Canopies.JPG
hero.caption: South view of the historic Helen P. Gay Rocky Mount (Amtrak station) in Rocky Mount, North Carolina canopies along the platform as taken from the corner of Nothwest Main Street and Hammond Street. Originally a Wilmington and Weldon Railroad then acquired by the Atlantic Coast Line Railroad, and restored for Amtrak. This shows three of the four stories of the station house and the two canopies along the platform, one of which leads directly to the station. This is a better shot of the canopies than the one I took of File:Rocky Mount Amtrak; Northwest View.JPG, but it doesn't show all four floors.

images.filename: 3-Di Sign on NC 4 that still includes Kenly.jpg
images.caption: Three-Line Distance Sign along eastbound North Carolina Highway 4 east of the southern end of the overlap with North Carolina Highway 48 north of Rocky Mount, North Carolina. NC 4 does not reach the City of Wilson, let alone Kenly, but the reason that it's listed as one of the destinations is because the sign dates back to the time when this segment of NC 4 was part of the decommissioned Rocky Mount and Wilson Business Route of Interstate 95 between 1978 and 1986.
images.alt: Three-Line Distance Sign along eastbound North Carolina Highway 4 east of the southern end of the overlap with North Carolina Highway 48 north of Rocky Mount, North Carolina.
